caveats: Research date 2026-09-27. PART A: 16 entries returned (target ~14). Only the near-term launches (Starship Flight 14, Crew-13, NROL-97, Starlink 15-25, MMX) have firm published times; everything from ~Oct 7 onward is 'NET' (no earlier than) or month-only and subject to slip - dates/times beyond ~Oct 10 are planning dates, not confirmed windows. Two manifest inconsistencies were resolved in favour of the more current source: (a) an older cached NextSpaceflight view showed Starship Flight 14 as Sep 18, but Spaceflight Now and SpaceX.com (updated late Sep) both show NET Sep 28; (b) an older cached SpaceX page listed Crew-13/Transporter-18 in a different order - SpaceX's live page shows Transporter-18 at Oct 1 11:18 PT and NROL-97 at Oct 1 23:53 ET (= Oct 2 03:53 UTC). Crew-13 agency attribution follows Spaceflight Now, which lists Joshua Kutryk as CSA. Chinese Long March and Russian manifests beyond Progress MS-36 are largely unreleased publicly, so the Q4 list skews heavily toward US launches; many additional Starlink/national-security Falcon 9 flights will fill the gaps but are not yet dated. PART B: 2025 and 2026 launch totals differ by tracker because of definitional choices (McDowell counts 3 near-orbital Starship flights; SpaceNews excludes them) - ranges given. The 2026 YTD figure (227) is a live counter and is already out of date. Soyuz family total (~1,150) is a sum of a variant table whose active-variant counts are only partially updated. Cumulative humans-flown (781) is as of April 2026 and counts suborbital fliers; definitions of the space border (FAI 100 km vs US 80 km) shift this number. Space-tourism pricing is opaque: Blue Origin has never published a price, and Virgin Galactic's headline price predates its post-2024 pause; figures given are the best documented. Note the two search tools available (Parallel Search MCP and DeepSeek web_search) were rate-limited/key-less during this session, so most data was gathered via direct fetches of the authoritative pages listed above.
